statement: The oldest fossil confidently attributed to genus Homo is LD 350-1, a partial mandible with five teeth from Ledi-Geraru, Afar, Ethiopia, dated 2.80-2.75 million years ago via argon-argon (⁴⁰Ar/³⁹Ar) dating of bracketing volcanic tephra layers combined with tephrostratigraphic and magnetostratigraphic correlation.

sources.citation: Villmoare, B., Kimbel, W.H., Seyoum, C., et al. "Early Homo at 2.8 Ma from Ledi-Geraru, Afar, Ethiopia." Science 347(6228): 1352-1355.
sources.author: Villmoare et al.

sources.citation: DiMaggio, E.N., Campisano, C.J., Rowan, J., et al. "Late Pliocene fossiliferous sedimentary record and the environmental context of early Homo from Afar, Ethiopia." Science 347(6228): 1355-1359.
sources.author: DiMaggio et al.
